thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: continuous-batcher OOM spike detected in us-east-2 (cluster: runtime-prod). Auto-pageback engaged, several containers crashed. Ticket created: INC-2026-3421
kevin: seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_PAGE_FAULT` in the batcher logs, looks like pagefaults during KV prefetch. stack excerpt:
```
2026-03-12T14:02:03Z batcher[pid=2143] ERROR cuda: CUDA_ERROR_PAGE_FAULT at 0x7f3a12c00000
    at batcher::kvcache::prefetch (kvcache.cc:412)
    at batcher::accumulator::flush (accumulator.cc:220)
```
kevin: multiple nodes affected, node-7 and node-12 showing container restarts. memory pressure + GPU page faults.
sanjay: ugh. could be GPU driver/firmware or bad kernel memory access when prefetching. first mitigation: disable kvcache prefetch on the batcher config and lower max_batch_size to 8. can someone roll that?
linda: on it. preparing a config patch to flip `kvcache.prefetch=false` and `batcher.max_batch_size=8` for the runtime-prod group. will push to canary first.
mike: customer impact? any 5xx or latency alerts from front door?
kevin: yes, several customers report 5-10s tails, a few timeouts. We've seen increased error rates for tokenization requests that hit the overloaded batcher. internal metric: batcher_queue_latency p50->p95 jumped from 120ms to 5.2s in the last 4m.
ash: (reacts) :eyes:  // note: user 'nash' not in participants list so ignore
ashley: I can take node drain for node-7 after the config change. recommend cordon + drain then restart container runtime.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: PATCH /runtime-configs/batcher/production -> set kvcache.prefetch=false, max_batch_size=8. Change will go to canary runtime-prod-canary-1. CI checks passed.
kevin: thanks. Linda, please apply canary, we'll watch pagefault logs and GPU error rate. If canary replicates, roll to all nodes.
linda: canary applied at 14:05Z. logs: small reduction in prefetch attempts but pagefaults still happening on canary node-1 (different node type). snippet:
```
2026-03-12T14:06:12Z batcher[pid=1987] WARN kvcache: prefetch failed, attempted pages=16, error=CUDA_ERROR_PAGE_FAULT
```
linda: rolling back prefetch change; trying alternative: set `kvcache.prefetch=false` + `batcher.prefetch_worker_count=0` + reduce `batcher.prefetch_window=0` to fully disable.
sanjay: also suggest turning on fallback routing to smaller model variant on overload: route_policy.on_overload -> model-variant-quantized. avoids large KV prefetches.
mike: good. Kevin, Ashley — please coordinate customer notifications. Which customers hit timeouts?
kevin: affected customers (observed errors in APM): "billing-ai", "chatflow", "notesync-enterprise". billing-ai had 4 user-facing timeouts in the past 6m. severity: S2 for billing-ai (customer SLA), rest S3.
ashley: starting handoff notes for next oncall in 28m. Actions taken: canary applied (partial), drain scheduled for node-7 after second config push, restart batcher container on node-12 manually. Observed container restart log: `killed by OOM\n` then `docker: container exited code=137`.
oncall-bot: oncall rotation: @sanjay will be primary in 28 minutes. Please add to handoff.
kevin: I manually restarted batcher on node-12, container came back but GPU driver logs show `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79` which matches page faults. I'm opening a driver escalation with infra team (cc @sre).
nash: (reaction) :+1:
ashley: after restart, batcher memory use dropped ~22% on node-12. latency improved slightly but not stable. continuing drain on node-7 now.
kevin: while we do that, I disabled continuous-batcher prefetch and set `batcher.max_inflight_requests=64` to reduce concurrency. pushing config cluster-wide as emergency throttle.
sanjay: if pagefaults are driver-related, we should fail fast to fallback model rather than attempt prefetch. set routing fallback to model-variant-quantized with immediate cutover if node GPU errors > threshold.
linda: done. routing fallback rule added: `on_gpu_error_rate>=0.1 -> fallback=quantized-v2`.
mike: customer comms: I'll draft a status update to SRE channel and customer success for billing-ai. Ashley, please capture exact error counts and attach logs.
ashley: attaching logs to ticket INC-2026-3421. Summary so far: 1) canary config applied 14:05Z, 2) further disable prefetch and throttle concurrency 14:09Z, 3) manual restarts on node-12 complete 14:11Z, 4) drain node-7 in progress 14:12Z.
deploy-bot: rollout succeeded: cluster-wide throttle applied at 14:09Z. No CI jobs failed.
kevin: post-throttle metrics: pagefault rate down 74%, container restarts fell to 0 in last 6m. batcher_queue_latency p95 back to ~480ms. Timeouts for billing-ai stopped after fallback routing engaged.
sanjay: nice. still want to escalate driver issue with infra and get kernel/driver stacktrace from node-7 (dmesg + nvflare logs).
mike: agree — action items: 1) infra: driver escalation with kernel dumps, 2) runtime team: reproduce prefetch memory access locally with synthetic workload, 3) product: notify billing-ai POC.
kevin: I'll keep the incident open for follow-up and create a playbook entry for disabling prefetch on load and for fallback routing.
nashley: handoff to @sanjay in 18m. nothing else critical right now. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: @sanjay primary in 18 minutes. If you accept, post `@oncall accepted` to this thread.
sanjay: @oncall accepted. I'll take over monitoring and the infra driver escalation.
mike: thanks all — prep a short RCA draft after infra analysis. Marking this as mitigated for customer impact at 14:18Z, but incident remains open for root cause. :memo:
